items.title: *15 Best Things I Bought In 2026*
items.content:
Hello and welcome to the first round-up of the season! Today, I will be sharing my top 15 things I bought this year.

*!*Next week will be the top 15 things readers bought! You’re gonna love it. I wanted to buy all that shit. I will still add a few more selections if you email them to me BY WEDNESDAY *!*

But today is about and stuff that I bought. Nothing in this newsletter is sponsored! I wish sponsors were sending me things, but they are not. These are all things I bought with my because I have when in

I’m aware that very few of these things are cheap. Do not add up how much all of these things cost. I haven’t done it and I refuse to. It was a bad year, sue me! But let my mistakes be your shopping list. All of these things would be great gifts and it is the gift buying season!

  1. My angel granny dog Georgia turns 13 soon. And in her old age, she contracted a bout of pancreatitis, which meant she had to eat rice for every meal for a few weeks. This was fine except my rice cooker was broken, so I bought a new really fancy one and now I’m addicted to it too! I love that it sings a song and keeps the rice warm for days.

  2. When Georgia was sick, I also bought her this Molly Mutt dog bed. Should I have purchased this when she already has so many beds? Probably not, but the purchase turned out to be justified because she loves it and clearly prefers it over all of her other beds.

  1. Because everything was so bad last winter, we decided to take a short little weekend away at THE STOCKTON INN in New Jersey. I cannot say enough about how nice this hotel was. The hospitality was personal. The tub was ginormous. I keep thinking about the food we ate in the restaurant. Highly recommend for anyone on the east coast looking for a weekend away. It’s pet friendly, also, and they gave Georgia a special ceramic water bowl. I would die for the Stockton Inn.

  2. I bought a little stool with a stained glass eggplant in it from Philadelphia artist Mary Tsai. It’s so whimsical and silly and I love it.

  1. I put a photo of The Boston General Store Fish Clips in a newsletter earlier this year, and a bunch of you responded saying they were great and I should buy them. SO I DID! And guess what? They are great! I’ve used them to keep chips closed, and papers together, and even as a bookmark in a pinch. Great little stocking stuffer too.

  1. I cook a lot of chicken thighs and the Thermapen thermometer is the best cooking thermometer I’ve ever used. Great purchase. It’s also large which makes it harder for me to lose.

  2. My friends Liz & Ashley & Mary and I took a few classes at Butcher’s Sewing Shop in Philadelphia this year. I learned to use the machine, and make a quilt, and make a dress. I don’t really have the attention to detail that sewing rewards, but I loved learning and making shit!

  3. I know this is a baby and basic sewist take, but I bought the Singer Heavy Duty as my sewing machine and I’m in love with her!! Plus it’s on sale for Black Friday. If you want to learn to sew, this is a great starter machine (she says, as a beginner)

  1. Speaking of learning! I bought myself Spanish classes again this year. Truly, learning a language as an adult is one of the hardest but most fulfilling things I’ve ever done. I first started taking lessons on iTalki, which would be a good gift-card for someone.

  1. I finally upgraded from garbage toothbrushes they give me at the dentist to the most basic level Sonicare, and everyone was right: my teeth feel cleaner.

  2. While I was in Mexico, I bought these little green mezcal sipping cups at A Mesa Puesto. They’re so cute and I love the way they feel in my hands

  1. Friend of the newsletter (me) and brilliant esthetician (book her for facials) Jolie de Feis, gave me the Crown Affair Dry Shampoo powder for my birthday. Unfortunately, this whips. My hair looks better with it in than it does after I wash it, and the little brush applies it evenly so there’s no white cast. I love it because I hate showering.

  1. As a big purchase this year, I bought an original painting from Philadelphia artist Ariel Posh. I cannot wait to hang it in my home, and I smile just thinking about it. More than anything, in this terrible stupid AI world, I recommend purchasing real work from real artists you love.

  1. As a Christmas present, I bought my partner this Saint Davis custom sapphire (my birthstone!) signet ring. When it showed up in September, I was so excited that I gave it immediately. Whoops! Now I’ll have to buy something else. All of this guy’s designs are really gorgeous and he was a pleasure to work with.

Thank you so much for subscribing to this silly newsletter! If you bought something great this year, send it to me by Wednesday!

If you are sad there is nothing to read this week, consider Defector.com. I cried reading two articles last week, but you’ll have to guess which ones.
